summary: US-CH6: Reseller API — an external partner sells from shared inventory
description:
The last and largest slice: an external reseller sells from the same inventory as everyone else, with the same no-oversell guarantee and per-reseller attribution. This introduces a **third identity class** — a machine-to-machine partner credential, alongside staff sessions (ADR-042), internal tokens (ADR-043) and customer sessions (ADR-049) — and closes the known commerce→inventory channel seam.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A partner credential class exists: per-reseller API credentials, scoped to one organizer and one channel from the registry (US-CH1). Credentials are stored hashed, never recoverable, and are revocable. **An ADR records this identity class** and its relationship to the three existing ones.
- The reseller surface is a **contract operation, not an internal route** — per ADR-043's line, it declares `security:` in the OpenAPI document and is validator-enforced, not header-compared in a handler. It is reachable from the edge (unlike `/internal/`), so the gateway gains an external partner route.
- The partner may: read availability for its channel, hold, and confirm a sale. It may **not** read anything scoped outside its organizer+channel.
- **The commerce→inventory channel seam is closed for GA pools**: a sale naming a channel consumes *that channel's* allocation. Today `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:260-263` documents that channel is deliberately not forwarded to inventory, with the consequence that a reseller-channel sale takes reseller fees while eating public inventory. **Closing this will make some currently-succeeding reserves return 409** — that behavior change is intended, must be called out in the PR, and must be covered by a test that asserts the new refusal.
- **The seated half of the same seam stays with TKT-176 and is an explicit non-goal here.** `CreateSeatHold` admits against capacity alone and `SeatHoldCreate` has no `channel` field at all, so a seated claim ignores allocations entirely — a separate defect with its own display consequences, already ticketed. This story must not silently half-fix it: if the reseller surface is offered on a seated pool, it refuses rather than overselling the channel, and the refusal cites TKT-176.
- Per-reseller attribution: the claim and the order carry the channel and the reseller identity, so settlement (TKT-217/ADR-048) can already split by it.
- Rate limiting per ADR-051's per-subject/per-source discipline applies to the partner surface.
- Tests: an unauthenticated call is refused by the validator (not the handler); a credential scoped to channel A cannot hold on channel B; the no-oversell contention proof holds with a reseller participating; the seam-closure 409; and a revoked credential is refused immediately.

Quality gates: `make check` green; contention smoke extended with a partner participant; OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate; the identity-class ADR merged with the code.

Parent: TKT-17. Depends on US-CH1 (channel registry), US-CH3 (per-channel price — a reseller with its own price is the point) and US-CH4 (windows). Non-goals: reseller settlement reports (TKT-23), partner self-service onboarding UI, OAuth flows beyond a credential.

objective.note: The epic's headline COS: an external reseller sells from shared inventory with the same no-oversell guarantee and per-reseller attribution. Nothing of it exists today.

scope.note: IN: partner credential class + ADR, contract-declared external surface, availability/hold/confirm scoped to organizer+channel, the commerce→inventory seam closure, attribution, ADR-051 rate limiting. OUT: settlement reporting (TKT-23), partner onboarding UI, OAuth.

uncertainties.note: AUTONOMOUS-RUN WAIVER applies to the WORK, and the owner has additionally instructed that this ticket STOP BEFORE MERGE for a human to re-take Gates 2 and 3. The two shape decisions — (1) credential shape: hashed bearer vs mTLS vs signed requests; (2) whether the seam closure ships behind a per-organizer opt-in or unconditionally — are drafted by the agent and recorded in kind=plan-final, but they are presented to the owner at Gate 2 rather than self-approved. Resolved for shaping purposes: the questions are identified and owned, which is what the DoR item asks.

dependencies.note: Verified on the board at claim time: TKT-235, TKT-237 and TKT-238 are all Done (as are TKT-236 and TKT-239). Zero open blockers.

approach.note: ADR-043 decides the mechanism outright: a public partner API is a contract operation, so it declares security: and is validator-enforced — NOT the inline header comparison commerce uses on internal routes. Verified at claim time that catalog already runs the declared-security idiom. SEAM LOCATION CORRECTED: the shaping-time citation of server.go:260-263 was stale; the seam is the comment at server.go:303 and the hold body at server.go:646, plus the same text in commerce/api/openapi.yaml and the generated openapi_gen.go. GA/SEATED OWNERSHIP RESOLVED: TKT-240 takes the GA half, TKT-176 keeps the seated half — verified that SeatHoldCreate carries no channel field at all, so the seated half cannot be half-fixed by accident here; the reseller surface refuses on seated pools citing TKT-176.

first_slice.note: Credential + scoped availability/hold/confirm + seam closure in one slice. Splitting the seam closure out would ship a reseller API that oversells its own channel, which is the opposite of the COS.

success.note: COS above; the no-oversell-with-a-partner contention proof and the seam-closure 409 test are the load-bearing ones.

context_memo.note: Re-resolved at claim time rather than trusted: governingTests baked (it was ABSENT — the gap that failed TKT-235's gate twice), 4 post-bake ADRs added, all cited ADRs and all test names verified to resolve at HEAD, stale line numbers corrected, and the ADR-055 numbering collision recorded.

binding.rule: Money is represented as integer minor units + ISO currency code everywhere; floats are banned on money paths.

Money-relevant records land as immutable, hash-chained, signed journal entries from the first order; every ticket/entitlement state change is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order. No raw PII in any append-only record — pseudonymous IDs only.

governingAdrs.why: The guard line is contract operation vs internal route: a public partner API is a contract operation and must declare security: and be validator-enforced, not header-compared in a handler.
Public customer-surface rate limiting: per-subject and per-source limits — an external partner API needs the same treatment.
The inventory pool row is the single serialization point; no background sweeper may be required for correctness.

Channel codes are exact opaque strings — no normalization, no case folding; a registry must not introduce an FK from claims (historical attribution) nor a counter; release stays a clock_timestamp() predicate under the pool FOR UPDATE.
OpenAPI is the source of truth; generated code must be committed before the gate or check-generate reads the regen as drift.
Response validation is fail-closed; a response that drifts from the contract is a 5xx, not a silent pass.
Catalog owns rule and entity definitions; commerce owns pricing/fee/promo evaluation. A channel registry is a definition and belongs in catalog.
Staff identity/back-office sessions — one of the three existing identity classes the new partner credential must be positioned against.
Customer identity/storefront sessions — the second existing class; the partner credential is explicitly a third, not a reuse of either.
Settlement ledger — per-reseller attribution must land in a shape settlement can already split by.
Name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident' or 'secure': a hashed credential protects against credential disclosure at rest, not against a writer with DB access.

Landed after this mémo was baked (TKT-236). The back office reads the channel registry with its OWN catalog credential — the precedent for a narrowly-scoped, purpose-specific credential rather than a shared token. The partner credential is the same shape of decision one step further out.
Landed after this mémo was baked (TKT-238). Per-channel sales windows as DB-time predicates on the allocation row. Refusal precedence interacts: window → code → capacity.

Landed after this mémo was baked (TKT-239). TWO facts bind TKT-240: (1) the pool row lock serializes ONLY what is pool_id-scoped, so ANY per-reseller quota or cross-slot counter needs its own row lock and a MULTI-SLOT contention proof — a single-slot test will pass while it oversells; (2) refusal precedence is window → code → capacity in both claim paths, and a new reseller refusal must slot into that order deliberately, or a gated channel reads as a sellout exactly when the on-sale is busiest (TKT-238's finding).

Landed after this mémo was baked (security review). Extends ADR-051 to the on-sale write path. The partner surface is a write path and inherits this discipline; read it WITH ADR-051 rather than instead of it. (Note the number collision recorded in `reference`.)

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-17 capability row + US-015 non-goals (registry/pricing/windows stay in TKT-17)

THE SEAM, line numbers corrected at claim time (the shaping-time citation of :260-263 was STALE — that range is now unrelated HTTP plumbing). The comment explaining the deliberate omission is at server.go:303; the inventory hold body that omits channel is built at server.go:646. The same prohibition text also lives in services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml (~:518-530) and is baked into the generated openapi_gen.go (~:550-553), so closing the seam edits three places and requires a regen commit before the gate.

TKT-176 (open, Backlog) owns the SEATED half of the same seam. VERIFIED at claim time: SeatHoldCreate (openapi_gen.go:442-449) has organizer/slot/ticket_type/seat_identities/unit_amount/currency and NO channel field at all. TKT-240 takes the GA half only; the reseller surface must REFUSE on a seated pool and cite TKT-176 rather than half-fixing it.
ADR-043's own table: catalog already runs declared-security over 37 operations, so the contract-declared idiom is existing, not new

CREDENTIAL BLAST RADIUS — INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN is one shared value opening commerce refunds and inventory operational holds; the partner credential must NOT be that token, nor share its scope (TKT-190 proposed exactly this and it was caught at plan-review)

Gateway route table (routes map at main.go:29). Internal routes are 404'd at the edge; an external partner route is a new edge binding. The internal-denial loop registers only for prefixes under /api/.

REGISTRY DEFECT found at claim time, NOT this ticket's to fix but it blocks picking an ADR number: ADR-055 is used TWICE — ADR-055-on-sale-write-rate-limiting.md (from the 2026-08-10 security review, commit 1783c843) and ADR-055-presale-unlock-codes.md (TKT-239, commit 179034c7). Both Accepted, both cited from code. TKT-240's new identity-class ADR must therefore take ADR-056 and must NOT assume 055 is free. Flagged to the owner.

governingTests.name: TestCatalogSpecGuardsEveryUnsafeOperationAndOnlyThose
governingTests.invariant: In catalog's spec, every unsafe operation requires CatalogStaffWriteCredential and declares 401; every safe one must explicitly opt out with `security: []`. Derived from the spec in both directions, so it needs no list edit — but catalog's DOCUMENT-LEVEL default security (services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:21) means a new public/partner read inherits the staff credential unless it opts out.

governingTests.name: TestDeclaredCacheControlValuesUseRegisteredTiers
governingTests.invariant: CLOSED ALLOWLIST across all five specs. Three hardcoded things bite: `wantSpecs = 5` (a sixth service spec fails outright), `wantDeclarations` (every operation declaring a Cache-Control — INCLUDING on a 401 or 429 — must be listed; shrinking coverage also fails), and `freeFormAllowed` (closed: a new Cache-Control must be a single-valued enum component, not a bare string). It also hard-refuses `callbacks:`/`webhooks:` in a spec. This is the test that failed TKT-235 twice.

governingTests.name: TestMain / uncovered2xxOps + TestCatalogCoverageGateIsDeliberatelyUnitScoped
governingTests.invariant: EVERY documented 2xx operation in inventory/commerce/payments/access must be exercised through the running smoke stack, or the whole smoke suite fails. `coverageAllowlist` is currently EMPTY (verified) — TKT-240 adding an entry would be the first since it was drained, so prefer writing a real driver. `smokeCoverageGatedServices` is pinned exact-and-ordered against ADR-030.

governingTests.name: TestMain (catalog coverage)
governingTests.invariant: Catalog's equivalent, in its unit suite, with NO allowlist at all: a new catalog operation must have a happy-path unit test through `env.do`.

governingTests.name: TestTheEnumerationCoversEveryInternalRouteCommerceServes
governingTests.invariant: A hand-written table and the real chi router must describe the same /internal/ surface, both directions, with a `len(onRouter) < 8` floor. NOTE for this ticket: it walks ONLY /internal/ — a partner surface mounted at a non-/internal/ prefix in commerce is invisible to it. That is the shape of hole to watch, not a reason to relax.

governingTests.name: TestCredentialsAreDistinctRefusesEveryCollidingPair
governingTests.invariant: Commerce's credentials must hold pairwise-distinct values, enumerated exhaustively. A FIFTH commerce credential (a partner secret) requires extending the signature AND adding every new pair — the file says a credential added to the wiring but not the check is the one whose separation is never verified.

governingTests.name: TestGatewayDeniesGenericInternalRoutes
governingTests.invariant: /api/<svc>/internal/* is 404'd AT THE EDGE with the gateway's own exact body. Hardcoded probe table. Related: gateway's internal-denial loop only registers for prefixes starting with `/api/` — a partner prefix outside /api/ silently gets no internal denial.

governingTests.name: TestBackofficeRoute / TestEncodedSeparatorCannotReachInternalRoutes / TestAForgedXForwardedForDoesNotReachTheUpstream
governingTests.invariant: The only unit-level pin of the gateway `routes` map; encoded-separator denial; and — load-bearing for ADR-051 rate limiting — the proxy REPLACES X-Forwarded-For with the connecting peer, which is what makes a per-source limit non-forgeable.

governingTests.name: TestCommittedServiceContractsAreComplete
governingTests.invariant: Every operation needs a non-empty operationId and EVERY response of every operation needs a committed body schema — including a new 401 and 429.

governingTests.name: TestNoProductionCodeUpdatesOrderAttribution + TestTheAllowlistCannotBeWidened + TestOrderSQLIsWrittenAsLiterals
governingTests.invariant: An AST scan of all commerce production Go: exactly TWO SQL statements may write orders.customer_id, matched whole-text including predicates, and order SQL must be written as literals so the scanner can see it. Directly in TKT-240's path: per-reseller attribution on the order. A new order INSERT built by string concatenation fails here.

governingTests.name: TestEveryStoreMethodIsClassifiedForPublicReads
governingTests.invariant: Every method on catalog's store.Store interface must be classified in `readOnlyStoreMethods` or `publicReadEffect`. Applies only if partner credential storage lands in catalog.

governingTests.name: TestMigrationsAppliedOutOfBand + TestMigrationsRanBeforeServicesStarted + TestServerModeDoesNotMigrate
governingTests.invariant: ADR-022: migrations run out-of-band as a Compose job the service waits on; the server path never migrates. Migration filenames are gate-enforced as NNNN_name.sql. NOTE: there is NO migration-number collision test — `max(version_id)` would not detect two files sharing a prefix; goose refuses only at apply time inside the smoke stack. Check the next free number by hand.

governingTests.name: TestCreateHoldRejectsBadChannel
governingTests.invariant: Inventory already validates channel_code on holds and engages the allocation cap. Forwarding channel from commerce (the seam closure) engages this 409 path — which is the intended breaking change.

governingTests.name: TestOnSaleWritesAreRateLimitedSeparatelyFromSignIn
governingTests.invariant: The SHAPE a new limiter must follow: prove the budget is finite AND that it is a separate bucket from neighbouring surfaces. There is NO repo-wide test asserting which routes must have a limiter — ADR-051 coverage on the partner surface is a discipline the plan must carry, not something the gate will catch. Also: a 429 must be DECLARED in the spec or ADR-028 fail-closed turns it into a 500.

governingTests.name: check-generate (Makefile target, not a Go test)
governingTests.invariant: Regenerated openapi_gen.go / api-types.gen.ts must be COMMITTED BEFORE the gate — it diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift. The seam's prohibition text is baked into services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go, so editing the OpenAPI description alone fails the gate until regenerated.

context.reResolvedAt: 2026-08-10 (claim-time re-resolution: all 11 original governingAdrs verified to resolve at HEAD; 4 ADRs added; governingTests baked from absent; every test name verified with `git grep -n "func Test..."` at HEAD; the seam's line numbers corrected)

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⚠️ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | ✅ | The epic's headline COS |
| Scope | ✅ | Credential + scoped surface + seam closure; settlement reporting stays TKT-23 |
| Uncertainties | ⚠️ | Two auth-shape decisions, normally `owner: human` — waived to the agent for this run by explicit owner instruction |
| Dependencies | ⚠️ | Blocked by TKT-235, TKT-237, TKT-238 |
| Approach | ✅ | ADR-043 decides the mechanism outright; verified the declared-security idiom already exists in catalog |
| First slice | ✅ | Splitting the seam closure out would ship a reseller API that oversells its own channel |
| Success | ✅ | Contention-with-partner and seam-closure-409 tests are load-bearing |
| Context-mémo | ✅ | Baked, incl. the INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN blast-radius entry (TKT-190's worked example) |

**Concerns:**
1. **New auth surface, externally reachable.** A third identity class. Normally `approach: deferred` would be refused here outright (shaping.md's four-surface exception); it is `met` because ADR-043 already decides the mechanism, and the residual shape questions are recorded as waived-to-agent rather than hidden.
2. **Intended breaking behavior change.** Closing the commerce→inventory seam turns some currently-succeeding reserves into 409s. Intended, tested, and called out — but it is the highest-blast-radius change in the epic.
3. **Data migrations** on the inventory hot path.
4. Blocked by three siblings.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — the largest and riskiest child. Proceeding under the owner's explicit waiver of stop-condition (b); every overridden objection is recorded in the closeout's `overrides:` list.

### Re-shaping at claim time — verdict: READY, with the merge gate restored

The mémo was baked 2026-08-09. This is the claim-time re-resolution the skill requires (never trust
a handoff's or a prompt's account of a ticket's state). Five things changed.

| Criterion | Was | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Objective | ✅ | ✅ | unchanged |
| Scope | ✅ | ✅ | unchanged |
| Uncertainties | ⚠️ open | ✅ | The two auth-shape decisions are identified and owned. They are **drafted** by the agent but **presented at Gate 2**, not self-approved — see below. |
| Dependencies | ⚠️ open | ✅ | TKT-235 / TKT-237 / TKT-238 all verified **Done** on the board. Zero open blockers. |
| Approach | ✅ | ✅ | Kept, but **corrected** — see finding 1. |
| First slice | ✅ | ✅ | unchanged |
| Success | ✅ | ✅ | unchanged |
| Context-mémo | ✅ | ✅ | Kept, but **substantially rebuilt** — see findings 2–4. |

#### 1. The COS cited a stale seam location, and it is corrected

The description cites `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:260-263`. That range is now unrelated
HTTP plumbing. Verified at HEAD (`a3b947e8`), the seam is:

- `server.go:303` — the comment explaining the deliberate omission
- `server.go:646` — where the inventory hold body is built without `channel`

And it is in **three** places, not one: the same prohibition text is in
`services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` (~:518-530) and is **baked into the generated**
`services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` (~:550-553). Closing the seam therefore edits the
spec and requires a **committed regen before the gate** — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD.

#### 2. The GA / seated ownership question, resolved rather than assumed

The code comment says *"TKT-176 owns that question"*; TKT-240's COS claims the seam. Resolved:
**TKT-240 takes the GA half, TKT-176 keeps the seated half.** This is not a silent reassignment —
the COS already scopes the seated half out as an explicit non-goal, and the code independently
confirms the split is clean: `SeatHoldCreate` (`openapi_gen.go:442-449`) carries organizer, slot,
ticket type, seat identities, unit amount and currency, and **no `channel` field at all**. The
seated half therefore cannot be half-fixed here by accident. The reseller surface **refuses** on a
seated pool and cites TKT-176.

#### 3. `governingTests` was ABSENT from the mémo — now baked (15 entries)

This is the gap that failed **TKT-235's gate twice**: a plan can be correct against every governing
ADR and still fail, because these invariants are discoverable only by failing the gate. Every name
below was verified to resolve at HEAD with `git grep -n "func Test…"`. The ones most likely to bite:

- **`TestDeclaredCacheControlValuesUseRegisteredTiers`** (`shared/go/cachetier/spec_audit_test.go`) —
  a **closed allowlist**. `wantDeclarations` must list every operation declaring a `Cache-Control`
  *including on a 401 or 429*; `freeFormAllowed` is closed; and it **hard-refuses `callbacks:`** in a
  spec.
- **`smoke/coverage_test.go`** — every documented 2xx operation in inventory/commerce/payments/access
  must be driven through the running stack or the whole smoke suite fails. `coverageAllowlist` is
  **empty** (verified) — an entry here would be the first since it was drained, so write a driver.
- **`TestNoProductionCodeUpdatesOrderAttribution`** — exactly **two** SQL statements may write
  `orders.customer_id`, matched whole-text, and order SQL must be **literals** so the AST scanner can
  see it. Per-reseller attribution walks straight into this.
- **`TestCredentialsAreDistinctRefusesEveryCollidingPair`** — a fifth commerce credential requires
  extending the signature *and* every new pair.
- **No repo-wide test asserts which routes must have a rate limiter.** ADR-051 coverage on the
  partner surface is a discipline the plan must carry; the gate will not catch its absence. And a
  `429` must be **declared** in the spec or ADR-028 fail-closed turns it into a 500.
- **No migration-number collision test exists** — `max(version_id)` cannot see two files sharing a
  prefix. Check the next free number by hand.

#### 4. Four ADRs landed after the bake, and one is a numbering collision

Added to `governingAdrs`: **ADR-053** (a narrowly-scoped purpose-specific credential — the direct
precedent), **ADR-054** (window → code → capacity refusal precedence), and **both** ADR-055s.

⚠️ **Registry defect, not this ticket's to fix but it blocks picking a number:** `ADR-055` is used
**twice** — `ADR-055-on-sale-write-rate-limiting.md` (security review, `1783c843`) and
`ADR-055-presale-unlock-codes.md` (TKT-239, `179034c7`). Both Accepted, both cited from code.
TKT-240's identity-class ADR must take **ADR-056** and must not assume 055 is free.

From ADR-055-presale: **the pool row lock serializes only what is `pool_id`-scoped.** If TKT-240 adds
any per-reseller quota or cross-slot counter it has the same problem, and a single-slot contention
test will pass while it oversells. TKT-239's proof uses three slots.

#### 5. The merge gate is restored for this ticket

The epic ran under an owner waiver of all four human gates. **This ticket stops before merge.** Six
consecutive closeouts recommended it and the owner has now instructed it. Reasons: a **third machine
identity class**, externally reachable; an **intended breaking change** that turns currently-succeeding
reserves into 409s; and TKT-239 having just demonstrated the failure mode where a confidently
reasoned plan decision was wrong *and the test asserted the defect as correct*
(`docs/learnings/2026-08-10-a-green-test-can-bless-the-defect.md`).

**Verdict: READY.** All 8 DoR items `met`, zero open blockers. Gate 1 is the owner's to clear.
